analysis.title: Walmart Inc 3Q Preview: Well positioned for durable growth
key_insights: BofA reiterates Buy on WMT with a $139 price objective (raised from $126), based on 44x F28E adjusted EPS, up from 40x, due to rerating in peer multiples. Price at writing was $125.55.
BofA expects WMT to update FY sales and EPS guidance to the upper end of its prior range with the 3Q report.

BofA's 3Q forecast includes +2.8% WMT US comps ex-fuel. After the recent sector rotation, it says the market needs to see an acceleration in WMT US comps ex health and wellness, and confidence that marketplace and advertising can accelerate EPS growth next year.

Rising oil prices are pushing up commodity costs and vendors are starting to raise prices. BofA thinks grocery inflation expectations have risen 50-100bp, with price increases recognized over the next 6-12 months. It sees the risk of demand pullback in general merchandise as low given WMT's value focus.

BofA argues WMT is the biggest winner in its coverage from greater agentic commerce adoption. This quarter WMT expanded Sparky to process pictures, added a 'shop to light' in-store location tool, and launched Agent Profiles, which let consumers authorize AI agents to shop with spending controls.

Advertising is a key pillar of the bull case. BofA expects momentum to continue, with the quarter including the Vibe.co acquisition. Marketplace grew +52% in 2Q, and BofA estimates marketplace sellers spend 10-12% of GMV on advertising versus 4-6% for Walmart suppliers.
BofA estimates Food at Home inflation was +2.1% in F3Q (Aug-Oct). Exhibit 2 shows SNAP benefits down year over year, leaving lower-income consumers with less cash.

market_movers.rationale: BofA raised its PO to $139 from $126 on a 44x P/E (from 40x) after peer multiples rerated. It expects continued grocery and general merchandise share gains and guidance at the upper end of the prior range.

sector_views.rationale: BofA sees WMT's omni-channel transformation supporting positive US comps with positive traffic, ecommerce and GMV growth, and P/E expansion.

earnings_insights: WMT 3Q (Aug-Oct) preview: BofA forecasts EPS of $0.63 (BofA estimate, not yet reported), versus $0.62 reported in 3Q last year. BofA's 4Q estimate is $0.77 versus $0.74 reported.
BofA forecasts +2.8% WMT US comps ex-fuel for 3Q (BofA estimate).
BofA expects FY sales and EPS guidance to be raised to the upper end of the prior range (BofA expectation).
BofA FY2027 (Jan) EPS estimate is $2.87, versus Bloomberg consensus $2.89 and Visible Alpha $2.88. FY2028 estimate is $3.15 versus consensus $3.22 (Bloomberg) and $3.21 (Visible Alpha).
FY2027E sales are $753.7B (+5.7%), with EBITDA of $49.6B (+9.7%) and adjusted net income of $22.9B (+8.1%), all BofA estimates.
2Q marketplace growth was +52%. 2Q EPS was $0.81 versus BofA's prior-year $0.68, and 1Q EPS was $0.66 (both reported).

macro_indicators.indicator: Food at Home CPI inflation (F3Q, Aug-Oct)
macro_indicators.interpretation: BofA's estimate. BLS did not publish Oct 2025 data, so BofA averaged Sept and Nov CPI to estimate the Oct 2025 base.
BofA thinks higher oil and vendor price increases will lift grocery inflation. This supports WMT sales, with a low risk of reduced general merchandise demand.

risk_factors: WMT's longer-term ability to keep gaining share given its size.
Competitive pressure at Sam's Club and/or Walmart International.
Higher inflation could raise elasticity and cut general merchandise demand, though BofA sees this as low risk.
Advertising model risk from greater agentic commerce adoption.
Lower-income consumers have less cash on a recalibration of SNAP benefits.
charts_described: Exhibit 1 compares Food at Home CPI with Walmart US reported grocery inflation, with BofA estimating Food at Home inflation at +2.1% in F3Q (Aug-Oct).
Exhibit 2 plots SNAP benefits year over year from Jan-23 to Oct-26, per the Daily Treasury Statement and USDA.

tension_points.bull_case: BofA's 44x multiple reflects positive US comps with positive traffic and tech-led share gains, with operating income growth nearly double the pace of sales growth.
tension_points.bear_case: The 44x target multiple is above WMT's 36x two-year average forward P/E. The market needs to see an acceleration in US comps ex H&W and in EPS growth from marketplace and advertising.
tension_points.what_invalidates: Slowing food inflation or deflation, or loss of incremental market share, would undermine the premium multiple.
